Today’s read
The biggest names carried the session. The fifty most traded stocks returned +10.23% weighted by turnover, against +0.06% for the median stock, a gap of 10.2 percentage points, so most stocks did worse than the busiest names suggest.

Syngene International Limited rose 12.2% on 69 times its usual volume. Its exchange filing that session was about guidance or investor update, “Investor Presentation”.

Ramky Infrastructure Limited rose 17.4% on 196 times its usual volume, and it was in the news with “Ramky Infrastructure shares surge over 17% to ₹300 despite a 46% yearly fall; what explains the sharp rebound?”.

Bajaj Electricals Limited rose 3.9% on 62 times its usual volume, and it was in the news with “Auto biggies Q2 result compared: Bajaj Auto vs Maruti Suzuki - Who wins the earnings race? Profit, revenue, target price”.

Aarti Drugs Limited rose 11.3% on 82 times its usual volume, and it was in the news with “Lab Rats series: Unlocking the kidney for therapy with Helex”.

What happened
Breaking
US Federal Reserve Keeps Interest Rates Unchanged - صحيفة مال
The Federal Reserve maintained the target federal funds rate at 5.25% to 5.50%. Higher US yields narrow the spread against Indian sovereign bonds, slowing foreign portfolio flows into domestic equities. A stronger dollar also depreciates the rupee, increasing landing costs for domestic crude refiners and net importers. US non-farm payroll data will confirm the interest rate trajectory.
Fed and rates
Federal Reserve keeps rates unchanged despite high inflation - Transport Topics
The Federal Reserve kept interest rates unchanged as US core CPI stayed above target levels. Sustained high US borrowing costs maintain elevated global equity discount rates, constraining foreign portfolio inflows into Indian equities. A firm dollar weighs on the rupee, threatening import-heavy sectors like chemical synthesis and electronics manufacturing. Upcoming US PCE inflation data will confirm policy duration.
Fed and rates
US Federal Reserve holds interest rates steady as stubborn inflation puts future rate hikes in focus
The US Federal Reserve held rates steady while warning that stubborn inflation could trigger further monetary tightening. Higher US borrowing costs delay rate cuts by the Reserve Bank of India, keeping interest expenses elevated for leveraged domestic capital goods and infrastructure companies. Brent crude spot prices rising above $85 per barrel will signal whether energy costs compel further Fed hikes.

Ramky Infrastructure shares surge over 17% to ₹300 despite a 46% yearly fall; what explains the sharp rebound?
Ramky Infrastructure rallied 17.4% to ₹300 with trading volume reaching five times the weekly average. The volume spike reflects short-term liquidity momentum rather than operational turnaround, as the stock remains down 46% year-to-date. Leveraged engineering construction sector valuations remain constrained by working capital requirements. Q2 order book disclosures will confirm whether underlying execution has improved.

Auto biggies Q2 result compared: Bajaj Auto vs Maruti Suzuki - Who wins the earnings race? Profit, revenue, target price
Bajaj Auto increased net profit by 35.2% on 34% revenue growth, while Maruti Suzuki saw net profit drop 26.4% despite 26% top-line growth. Two-wheeler makers are benefiting from export demand and premiumization margins, while passenger vehicle original equipment manufacturers face margin contraction due to higher marketing discounts and raw material costs. Upcoming monthly FADA dealer inventory numbers will confirm retail demand.

Your themes
Government extends PLI scheme for textiles until 2033-34 to boost MSME participation and investments
The textiles ministry extended the Production Linked Incentive scheme through 2033-34 while lowering minimum investment thresholds to draw smaller manufacturers. Lower qualifying hurdles let mid-tier fabric and garment makers claim fiscal payouts on man-made fibre and technical textile capex. Listed players like KPR Mill and Gokaldas Exports gain a wider runway to execute delayed capacity expansions without forfeiting state incentives.
Import substitutionET Economy
India’s Solar Cell Manufacturing Capacity Faces a Major Gap - Urban Acres
Domestic solar module capacity exceeds domestic solar cell manufacturing by roughly 30 gigawatts, forcing developers and assemblers to import cells. This structural deficit leaves module assemblers exposed to basic customs duties and volatile Chinese cell prices, compressing gross margins. Integrated players like Tata Power and Premier Energies benefit through captive cell supply, whereas unintegrated assemblers face continued margin pressure.

Exclusive-US DOJ is inquiring about Nvidias purchase of Hugging Face, sources say
The US Department of Justice opened an antitrust inquiry into Nvidia's investments in artificial intelligence platform Hugging Face. The regulatory review focuses entirely on US semiconductor distribution practices and developer ecosystem access. It carries no direct transmission mechanism to Indian equities, software exports, or domestic technology earnings.

This product showcase at a trade expo is routine marketing by a foreign supplier and has no financial or operational impact on Indian equities.

Waaree Energies reports INR 59,200 crore order book - pv magazine India
Waaree Energies disclosed an unexecuted order book of Rs 59,200 crore, providing nearly two years of revenue visibility for its module manufacturing business. Operating margins will depend on captive cell capacity and US import tariff determinations on Indian panels. Quarterly execution rates and export realisations in forthcoming filings will confirm whether this order intake converts into anticipated free cash flow.

From AI to cloud and connectivity from space: Akash Ambani announces Jio's plans to expand beyond affordable data
Reliance Jio outlined plans to direct future investments toward enterprise cloud services, artificial intelligence infrastructure, and satellite broadband. The strategy keeps capex elevated at parent Reliance Industries, deferring net debt reduction and free cash flow generation from the telecom segment. Enterprise cloud deal wins over the next four quarters will test whether these capital outlays produce accretive returns on capital.

Waaree Renewable Technologies Secures 450 MWp Solar EPC Order For FY2027–28 Completion - SolarQuarter
Waaree Renewable Technologies secured a 450 megawatt-peak solar engineering, procurement, and construction order scheduled for completion in FY28. The win reinforces execution visibility for the capital goods firm and highlights sustained utility-scale solar ordering by power developers. EBITDA margins on fixed-price EPC contracts remain the key metric to monitor in coming quarterly filings as equipment costs fluctuate.
Order wins and capex
Waaree Renewable Technologies secures EPC for 450 MWp solar project in Rajasthan - pv magazine India
This report repeats the 450 megawatt-peak solar EPC contract awarded to Waaree Renewable Technologies, specifying its location in Rajasthan. Regional grid connectivity and land acquisition timelines in Rajasthan will determine project commissioning speed. The execution schedule directly impacts revenue recognition timing for the company across the FY26 to FY28 accounting periods.

Jio Platforms IPO surge ends Tata's reign as India's most valuable group
Reliance Group total market valuation crossed ₹30 trillion following strong listing gains in Jio Platforms, surpassing Tata Group as India's most valuable corporate entity. Value unlocking in telecom and digital services lowers holding company discounts for parent conglomerates and alters sectoral weights in benchmark indices. Institutional asset allocation adjustments across large-cap holdings will confirm if this valuation shift holds.

Macro and economy
Sebi to review FPI compliance norms, issue consultation paper to align with global standards
Market regulator SEBI announced a consultation paper to simplify foreign portfolio investor compliance and align requirements with international benchmarks. Lowering operational friction and custodian costs directly improves capital mobility for overseas institutional funds entering Indian equity markets. Monthly net foreign portfolio investment flows and custodian registration figures will indicate whether these administrative changes boost foreign participation.
ET Markets · +1 other
Fed holds rates, says data will guide next move
The US Federal Reserve kept interest rates unchanged, though two officials dissented in favor of an immediate rate hike. Higher foreign interest rate expectations support US Treasury yields, placing depreciation pressure on the Indian rupee and spurring capital outflows from emerging markets. US inflation prints and RBI foreign exchange reserve interventions will show if local liquidity tightens further.
ET Markets
HUL sales rise 15% to hit 14-quarter high, but inflation clouds demand outlook
Hindustan Unilever posted September quarter turnover of ₹18,071 crore, up 15% year-on-year, driven by 7% volume growth and 7.5% price increases. Strong 22% growth in homecare sustained overall revenue, though elevated input cost inflation poses risks to operating margins. Subsequent rural demand volume trends and palm oil price movements will confirm if consumer spending can absorb further price increases.
ET Markets
Union Cabinet approves ₹10,000 crore Container Manufacturing Scheme to boost India's production
The Union Cabinet approved a ₹10,000 crore incentive scheme to build domestic shipping container manufacturing capacity by 2040. This structural intervention addresses acute import dependence on Chinese containers, directly reducing freight cost volatility for Indian exporters. The subsidy outlay supports order visibility for listed logistics operators like CONCOR and specialty steel suppliers catering to container fabricators.

Companies and earnings
TVS Motor Q2 Results: Profit jumps 52% YoY to Rs 1,377 crore; revenue rises 44%
TVS Motor reported a 52% year-on-year increase in net profit to ₹1,377 crore for the second quarter, driven by a 44% revenue expansion. Volume growth in electric two-wheelers and premium motorcycles expanded operating margins despite higher battery cell input costs. The strong execution improves earnings visibility for two-wheeler OEMs and auto ancillary suppliers like Sona BLW and Endurance Technologies.
ET Markets
Wall Street ends higher as Fed holds key rate steady, focus turns to earnings
The US Federal Reserve kept its benchmark interest rate unchanged, stabilizing global liquidity conditions. A pause in US monetary tightening caps Treasury yields, checking capital outflows from emerging markets and supporting Foreign Portfolio Investment flows into Indian equities. Stable interest rate differentials relieve pressure on the Indian rupee and give the Reserve Bank of India room to retain domestic monetary policy flexibility.
Reuters Business
Alphabet shares fall over 10% after earnings miss as AI spending drives cash burn
Alphabet shares dropped 10% after accelerating artificial intelligence capital expenditure squeezed margins and outpaced digital ad revenue. Elevated infrastructure spending by global tech hyperscalers indicates sustained outsourced engineering demand for Indian IT services giants like TCS, Infosys, and Wipro. Continued capital allocation toward enterprise AI deployments directly supports order book conversion across Indian software exporters despite weaker discretionary ad budgets.
Hindu BusinessLine
Campari confirms 2026 outlook after 3.4% rise in third quarter revenue
This quarterly revenue update from a European spirits producer has no material transmission mechanism to Indian listed equities.
Reuters Business
Geopolitics
Canadian Oil Discount Exceeds $30 Amid Gulf Coast Pressures
Western Canadian Select heavy crude's discount to WTI widened past $30 per barrel, its largest gap in over four years. Wider heavy-light crude differentials lower input costs for complex Indian refiners like Reliance Industries and HPCL, expanding gross refining margins as their coking units process cheaper heavy grades into high-value distillates. Weekly Singapore GRM updates will show whether this heavy crude weakness spreads globally.
Mint Markets
Fed's Kevin Warsh says US economy not running too hot from AI boom
Federal Reserve official Kevin Warsh stated the US economy is not overheating despite heavy corporate investment in artificial intelligence. Stable US rate expectations protect capital flows into Indian equities and keep the rupee steady, while reassuring IT exporters like TCS and Infosys regarding sustained enterprise technology spending. Upcoming US non-farm payroll data will confirm if labor tightness threatens this monetary outlook.
